fields.meta_description: Build a rental agreement form tenants fill in and sign online, with every lease and its end date kept in a table you own. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Rental Agreement Form Tenants Fill and Sign Online
fields.hero_description: Describe the property and your terms. Emergent builds the rental agreement form, sends each finished agreement out for signature and keeps every lease in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a Rental Agreement Form Should Cover
fields.features_subheading: Every agreement rests on the same core terms. Emergent turns them into fields and keeps track of each lease once it is signed.
fields.feature_1:
Every term in its own field

Emergent asks for the parties, the address, the lease term, the rent with its due date and grace period, the late fee, the deposit, utilities, pets and who handles repairs.
fields.feature_2:
Your terms fixed, their details asked

Set the rent and house rules before the link goes out. Tenants fill in only their own part, starting with the legal name of every adult who will live there and a move-in date.
fields.feature_3:
A filled agreement ready to sign

Submitting the form produces the agreement as a PDF with every blank completed. Each party signs on screen, and the signed copy is emailed to everyone and stored with that lease.
fields.feature_4:
The right disclosures on each lease

Record when each property was built, and units from before 1978 get the lead paint disclosure and EPA pamphlet in their packet. Attach state or city addenda by property too.
fields.feature_5:
One table for every lease you manage

Each signed agreement becomes a row with its unit, tenants, rent and end date. Sort the table by end date or filter it by property, and get an email before any lease runs out.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, your source code

Publish the form on your own domain or link it from a rental listing. Export the full source to GitHub whenever a developer wants to add a tenant portal or online rent collection.

fields.usecase_heading: Rental Agreement Forms for Every Property
fields.tab_content_1:
House rules the tenant signs before move-in

One link goes to the new tenant of a spare room. They enter a move-in date and an emergency contact, then read the house rules: quiet after 10 pm, overnight guests for 3 nights at most. Rent is $950, due on the 1st. The agreement goes out for signature the moment they submit.
fields.tab_content_2:
Leases ending within 60 days surface first

Every lease at Birch Court sits in one table, sorted by end date. Anything ending within 60 days rises to the top, and the property manager gets an email to start the renewal conversation. All 48 units stay in one view instead of a folder of PDFs.
fields.tab_content_3:
Nothing is final until the last roommate signs

Each roommate on the lease gets a personal signing link and sees their share: $800 of the $2,400 rent. The landlord can see who has signed. Anyone still unsigned after two days gets a reminder, and the finished copy reaches all three once the last signature is in.
fields.tab_content_4:
Collect the damage deposit with the booking

Guests booking the lake house accept the stay rules on the same form they book with: check-in at 4 pm, checkout by 11 am, six guests at most. A $300 damage deposit is collected through Stripe, and the stay is confirmed only after the guest signs.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Rental Agreement Form
fields.howto_description: Settle the terms before you write a single field. Seven steps take you from that list to a published form that sends every agreement out for signature.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List the terms that never change
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Decide what the tenant fills in
fields.howto_step_1_des: List what stays the same for every tenant at this property: rent, due date, grace period, late fee, deposit, utilities, pets and repair duties. These become fixed text in the agreement, and no tenant can edit them when they fill in the form.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask only for what changes from one tenant to the next. Names of the adults on the lease and the move-in date are the core; add other occupants or vehicles if your rules depend on them. Keep income and background questions for a separate screening step.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Deposit limits and required disclosures vary by state. California, for example, caps most deposits at one month's rent and gives landlords 21 days after move-out to return them. Federal rules add a lead paint disclosure for most housing built before 1978.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Describe the property and paste your terms into the prompt. Emergent builds the form and the lease table that stores each signed copy. Change any wording later by asking in plain English, and the update goes live on the same link.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Choose who signs and in what order. Tenants usually sign first and the landlord countersigns last. Once every signature is in, the app emails the signed PDF to each party and attaches it to that lease's row in the table.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Add reminders for the lease term
fields.howto_step_6_des: Pick the moments that need a nudge, like an agreement still unsigned after two days or a lease close to its end date. Send each reminder by email or Slack to the person who acts on it, with a direct link to the record.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test it with a made-up tenant
fields.howto_step_7_des: Fill the form as a fictional tenant, sign as both parties and read the PDF line by line. Then have a local attorney review the agreement text before the first real tenant signs it. Fix anything they flag by prompting, and test once more.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Rental Agreement Form Tenants Fill and Sign Online', meta 'Free Rental Agreement Form Builder | Emergent' and hero cover the whole job: form, signature, lease records.

intent.evidence: Builder-fit SERP of government PDFs and template sites; feature_1 and howto_1 list every term a lease needs ('the parties, the address, the lease term, the rent with its due date and grace period...'), and all 10 FAQ items are live PAA questions.

specificity.evidence: Landlord vocabulary throughout: 'grace period', 'countersigns', 'lead paint disclosure and EPA pamphlet', 'Birch Court', '$800 of the $2,400 rent'; form-builder table has no specialist variant (QC Q4 clean).

openers.evidence: Every paragraph opens on a full sentence with a verb: 'Emergent asks for the parties', 'Set the rent and house rules', 'One link goes to the new tenant of a spare room', 'Guests booking the lake house accept'.

craft.evidence: Five ideas restated across fields with words swapped (CONTENT_DEFECTS #21): fixed terms vs tenant fields (feature_2, howto_step_1/2), signed copy emailed and stored (feature_3, howto_step_5), lease-end email (feature_5, tab_content_2, howto_step_6), check your state's rules (howto_step_3, FAQ 3, 5, 7, 10), lead paint before 1978 (feature_4, howto_step_3, FAQ 10).

voice.evidence: Calm, specific, unglamorous detail: 'quiet after 10 pm, overnight guests for 3 nights at most. Rent is $950, due on the 1st.' No AI tells, no hype.

truth.evidence: Unsourced statements of fact: FAQ 6 'Handwriting is rarely the issue; the terms and the signatures are.', FAQ 5 'its templates are written for local law', howto_step_5 'Tenants usually sign first and the landlord countersigns last.'; unsourced third-party claim FAQ 7 'It can draft the text of a lease agreement form in seconds.'

distinct.evidence: Own page: room rental, 48-unit building, roommate split, lake-house deposit; no sibling primary (lease renewal, tenant screening) used as a heading.

faq.evidence: The 'have a local attorney review it' advice appears three times: FAQ 3 'have a local attorney read the final text', FAQ 6 'A local attorney can confirm', howto_step_7 'have a local attorney review the agreement text' (CONTENT_DEFECTS #21).

images.evidence: One moment per tab, names and numbers match the copy ($950 due the 1st; Birch Court 48 units, 38 and 54 days; $800 of $2,400, Riley unsigned 2 days; 4 pm, 11 am, six guests, $300 via Stripe); cover and share read cleanly.

findings.quote: Handwriting is rarely the issue; the terms and the signatures are.
findings.issue: A legal-validity statement about handwritten leases with no entry in spec.domain_sources. The only sourced fact in that answer is California Civil Code 1624 (leases over one year in writing). Same class elsewhere: FAQ 5 'Check your county or state housing agency first, because its templates are written for local law.' (unsourced claim about agency templates); howto_step_5_des 'Tenants usually sign first and the landlord countersigns last.' (unsourced claim about common practice).
findings.fix: Source each claim (a state bar or court self-help page saying handwritten leases are enforceable when they hold the required terms and signatures; the same for signing order), or recast them: FAQ 6 can open on the sourced point ('A lease can be written by hand; what matters is that it holds the terms your state requires and is signed'), but only with a source behind it. Otherwise make the agency and signing-order lines recommendations ('Start with your county or state housing agency's template'; 'Have tenants sign first and countersign last').

findings.quote: It can draft the text of a lease agreement form in seconds. ... A chat draft also stays a document: it collects no tenant answers or signatures.
findings.issue: Two claims about a third-party system (ChatGPT's capability and its speed) with no entry in spec.domain_sources.
findings.fix: Add an OpenAI source for what ChatGPT does, or answer without characterising the product: 'It can produce a draft. Check every clause against your state's rules, and remember a draft collects no tenant answers or signatures until it becomes a form.' Drop 'in seconds'.

findings.quote: have a local attorney read the final text
findings.issue: The same advice in three fields with the words swapped: FAQ 3 'have a local attorney read the final text'; FAQ 6 'A local attorney can confirm whether a handwritten agreement covers your state's rules.'; howto_step_7_des 'have a local attorney review the agreement text before the first real tenant signs it.'
findings.fix: Say it once, in howto_step_7 where it belongs. FAQ 3 and FAQ 6 then add something new (FAQ 3: what a self-written lease must name; FAQ 6: the sourced writing requirement).

findings.quote: Deposit limits and required disclosures vary by state.
findings.issue: 'Check your state's deposit limits and disclosures' is restated in five fields: howto_step_3_des 'Deposit limits and required disclosures vary by state.'; FAQ 3 'add the disclosures your state requires'; FAQ 5 'Compare its deposit and notice terms with your state's rules before anyone signs it.'; FAQ 7 'Check every clause against your state's deposit limits and required disclosures before using it.'; FAQ 10 'Watch for a deposit above your state's limit'.
findings.fix: Keep the rule in howto_step_3 (with the California example). Give each FAQ answer its own content instead of the state-rules reminder.

findings.quote: units from before 1978 get the lead paint disclosure and EPA pamphlet in their packet
findings.issue: The pre-1978 lead paint disclosure appears in three fields: feature_4 'units from before 1978 get the lead paint disclosure and EPA pamphlet in their packet'; howto_step_3_des 'Federal rules add a lead paint disclosure for most housing built before 1978.'; FAQ 10 'A missing lead paint disclosure on an older building is another.'
findings.fix: Keep feature_4 (what the app does) and one other mention at most; replace the FAQ 10 red flag with a different one.

findings.quote: Set the rent and house rules before the link goes out. Tenants fill in only their own part, starting with the legal name of every adult who will live there and a move-in date.
findings.issue: The fixed-terms / tenant-fields split is said in feature_2 and again in howto_step_1_des 'These become fixed text in the agreement, and no tenant can edit them when they fill in the form.' and howto_step_2_des 'Names of the adults on the lease and the move-in date are the core'.
findings.fix: Let the how-to own the split. Feature_2 says something the steps do not, for example optional per-property questions (vehicles, occupants) shown only where the rules need them.

findings.quote: Each party signs on screen, and the signed copy is emailed to everyone and stored with that lease.
findings.issue: Restated in howto_step_5_des: 'Once every signature is in, the app emails the signed PDF to each party and attaches it to that lease's row in the table.'
findings.fix: Keep the delivery in one field; howto_step_5 can stay on choosing the signing order.

findings.quote: Sort the table by end date or filter it by property, and get an email before any lease runs out.
findings.issue: The lease-end email sorted by end date is restated in tab_content_2 'sorted by end date. Anything ending within 60 days rises to the top, and the property manager gets an email' and howto_step_6_des 'or a lease close to its end date'.
findings.fix: Tab 2 is the worked example; feature_5 can stay on the table itself (unit, tenants, rent, filters) and howto_step_6 on choosing who gets which reminder, without repeating the end-date email.

findings.quote: Other warning signs are repair duties pushed entirely onto the tenant and an automatic renewal clause with no notice period.
findings.issue: The red-flag list is best-practice guidance with no source. It is phrased as a recommendation, so it is a note.
findings.fix: Add a tenant-rights source (a state attorney general or HUD page) for the red flags, or keep them as advice.

findings.fix: Drop the chip from the image brief, or add the rule to tab_content_1.

findings.issue: The guest shares her name with a well-known living architect; IMAGE_BRIEF rule 6 asks for fictional people.
findings.fix: Use a plainly fictional name (for example Maya Lindqvist).

findings.issue: Mockup keys should be camelCase tab names; tab 3 is 'Shared Leases' (multiUnitBuildings vs 'Multi-Unit Buildings' is fine). The template matches by order, so nothing breaks.
